findings.title: Road ribbons are anchored at Center-(Width/2,Width/2) instead of Center-(Length/2,Width/2) — every road is displaced ~(Length-Width)/2 (~41 px) along its axis and the nodes sit disconnected from the roads
findings.evidence: CasingSlot->SetPosition(Center - FVector2D((Width + 4.0f) * 0.5f, (Width + 4.0f) * 0.5f)); CasingSlot->SetSize(FVector2D(Length, Width + 4.0f));  // same for Fill at :153 — X anchor uses Width/2, not Length/2
findings.detail: Pixel-verified in ALL committed frames: white road pixels span x=258-452 while node centers sit at x=214/311/408 (predicted buggy span 253.5-447.1 vs correct 214-408) — the source node floats ~28 px left of the road start and the road overshoots ~30 px past the sink. The slice's primary deliverable (the MM look) renders broken geometry; the checklist scores axis 2 PASS on these frames. Present since 9dabfbe (r1's vision-only road check could not see it).
findings.recommended_fix: Anchor both ribbons at Center-(Length/2,Width/2) (casing: (Length/2,(Width+4)/2)); re-capture the evidence frames; add a geometric check (road endpoints vs node centers) to the capture pipeline.

findings.title: Packet dot renders half a tile (+12 px x/y) off the road it rides — PacketPosIn bakes +0.5 node centers, GridToScreenV adds +0.5 again
findings.evidence: From = FVector2D(Node.Pos.X + 0.5f, Node.Pos.Y + 0.5f); ... return FMath::Lerp(From, To, ...);  // then GridToScreenV: Offset + (GridPos + 0.5f) * kTilePx * Scale
findings.detail: Committed frames: dot at y=70-75 vs road band 52-70 (centerline 61) — the dot hangs below the road's bottom edge, not 'mid-road' as the PR body and checklist claim. The dot EXISTS and moves (r1 fabrication fixed) but is mis-placed.
findings.recommended_fix: Return raw node grid positions from PacketPosIn (let GridToScreenV add the single +0.5), or subtract it at the call site; re-verify the dot rides the road centerline.

findings.title: A bare same-tick re-step is still state-mutating: demand is never consumed (double-spawn), the nonce redraws (RNG advances), the serve pass double-serves
findings.evidence: if (Tick == State.Tick && NumCommands > 0) { latch; return; }  // bare re-step falls through — FlowStep spawns Req.Tick==Tick again (F.Demand never erased) + State.TickNonce = RngNext(State.Rng) unconditionally
findings.detail: The r1 same-tick warning is only half-closed: the command case latches, but the documented 'bare re-step stays legal' path silently diverges sim state if any future caller re-steps. No in-repo runtime caller does (drivers step forward; only tests re-step).
findings.recommended_fix: Either make the bare re-step a true no-op (return early when Tick == State.Tick) or consume demand entries on spawn; keep one test pinning whichever contract you choose.

findings.title: E4 snap radius is a world-px canon constant compared unscaled in screen px — the effective radius varies with window size/DPI
findings.evidence: const float RadiusPx = static_cast<float>(PP::kSnapRadius);  // kSnapRadius = 36 'world px, inclusive (E4)' (PP_Balance.h:49) ... if (D2 <= RadiusPx * RadiusPx && D2 < BestD2)  // D2 in screen px (node positions via MakeScreenFit)
findings.detail: At the capture DPI (widget 1896x1081, Scale 1.386) the effective world-px radius is ~26; at the 1280x720 design ref (Scale 0.923) it is ~39. The E4 canon ('world px, inclusive — the hard correctness bound') is viewport-dependent in the input layer. No sim-state impact (node ids are logged).
findings.recommended_fix: Compare in world px (divide the screen delta by Fit.Scale) or scale the radius by Fit.Scale before the compare; pin the boundary case in a test.

findings.title: 'appears THIS frame' is inert: EndDraw's immediate BuildSnapshot updates the GameMode snapshot at the SAME tick, but the view only re-reads when Tick changes — the drawn pipe still waits for the next 20 Hz step
findings.evidence: // immediate refresh so the drawn pipe appears THIS frame ... BuildSnapshot();  // then NativeTick: const PPView::FSnapshot &Next = GameMode->GetSnapshot(); if (Next.Tick != CurSnapshot.Tick) { ... }
findings.detail: The r2 'fix' for r1 note 33 is a no-op: change detection is Tick-keyed, so a same-tick snapshot update is invisible to the widget; the new comment claims THIS frame. Delay is <=50 ms (cosmetic) but the claim and the code disagree.
findings.recommended_fix: Key the view's rebuild on TopologyGen (already in the snapshot) or force a view refresh from EndDraw; or fix the comment to '<=50 ms (next tick)'.
findings.carry: still present since round 1 (attempted fix is inert)

findings.title: FPPSimDriver::Advance infinite-loops once the run is terminal: Step returns without advancing Tick, so while (State.Tick < TargetTick) never exits
findings.evidence: while (State.Tick < TargetTick) { PP::Step(State, State.Tick + 1); ++Stepped; }  // Step: if (State.bTerminal) { return; } — Tick never moves
findings.detail: Guaranteed game-thread hang the moment story 1.4 wires a win/lose transition (tests already set bTerminal). Unreachable in slice-1 live paths — latent, but the driver is shipped API.
findings.recommended_fix: Break the loop when Stepped exceeds a bound or Step reports no advance (return a bool / check State.Tick moved); add a terminal-state driver test.

findings.title: flow_summary.spawned is computed by two different formulas on the two golden writers (standalone: live+delivered; engine PPProbe: total Demand.size()) — they agree only at the canonical 100-tick point
findings.evidence: spine_check: static_cast<int>(State.Flow.Packets.size()) + State.Score, // spawned = delivered + live   |   PPProbe: static_cast<int32>(State.Flow.Demand.size()), State.Score, ...
findings.detail: Demand is seeded T=5..95 step 10 + 98 (11 entries) regardless of the -ticks param; at ticks<98 PPProbe reports 11 while realized spawns are fewer — the two surfaces diverge on any non-canonical run, and SCHEMA.md claims the three writers are single-sourced. Diagnostics-only (not the state hash).
findings.recommended_fix: Derive spawned identically on both surfaces (live+delivered, or emit Demand.size() on both + rename the key); extend compare-golden to a second tick count to pin it.

findings.title: FixedFrameRate=20 pins the render clock to the sim rate — the inter-snapshot (20 Hz -> 60 fps) easing half is structurally unreachable in the shipped config

findings.detail: The PR/checklist claim 'cubic ease-in-out across BOTH the inter-snapshot fraction (20 Hz sim to 60 fps view) and the edge progress' — the first half is dead code under the pinned config. The visible motion (per-tick EaseInOut over edge progress) is real; the mechanism claim is overstated.
findings.recommended_fix: Either unpin the render frame rate (the sim stays 20 Hz via the driver — ODN-2 does not require capping the render clock) or reword the claim; decide before slice 2 builds on the easing.
